license_content.description: The share-alike layer for community-authored expressive content (characters, recaps). Kept in a separate def so a CC0 core record can never carry it and vice versa.

position.description: A spoiler position within a work's own timeline. chapter is the logical (edition-independent) work chapter, 1-based; 0 means front matter or knowledge carried from earlier books in a series.

genre.description: One entry from the project's own normalized genre vocabulary. It is a controlled list this project owns, not a retailer's taxonomy, so a value is only added by amending this enum.

genre_list.description: A work's genres: at least one entry, no duplicates, drawn from the controlled vocabulary.

credit_role.description: One contributor role from the project's own controlled vocabulary. Authorship and narration are deliberately absent: they are modeled by work.authors and recording.narrators, and a credit never restates them. The list is owned by this project (never a retailer's), starts from the roles the import sources actually attest, and grows only by amending this enum - which is additive, so a consumer that does not know a value can ignore it.

credit.description: One contributor credit: a person, in a stated role. The person is a slug into the people family, exactly like an author or a narrator.

credit_list.description: Role-qualified contributor credits. One person MAY appear several times in different roles (a source really does credit one person as 'editor and translator'), but never twice in the SAME role: uniqueItems rejects the exactly-repeated object and pkg/check's credit-pair rule reports it in human terms. ORDER IS NOT SIGNIFICANT and is not checked: unlike authors, whose order is the source's statement about billing, a credit list is a set of independent (person, role) facts. The importer nonetheless emits it sorted by (person, role) so one set of credits has one byte-form and a re-import is a no-op; a hand-written record is free to order it however reads best.

isbn_list.description: A flat list of ISBNs whose region is not modeled. This is the WORK's print-ISBN shape (xref.isbn); a recording's isbn[] is its own definition in recording.schema.json, whose entries may state the region a production was released under.

region.description: A marketplace region. One vocabulary shared by every region-scoped field (recording ASINs, region-scoped ISBNs, regional publishers) so the lists can never drift apart.

date_time_offset.description: An RFC 3339 date-time that states its UTC offset, e.g. 2026-07-12T18:23:45+01:00 or 2026-07-12T17:23:45Z. The offset is required: a local time with no offset is not a point in time.

date_or_datetime.description: Either a plain calendar date or a full RFC 3339 date-time with offset. Both shapes are accepted so the one-time git-history backfill can write commit timestamps verbatim - the release artifact's bytes must not change across the storage migration - while everything stamped afterwards is a plain date, as imported_at already is.
